top3.headline: Meng To builds a 3D city driving game in a day
top3.whyItMatters: Small teams with AI can now ship rich interactive work that once needed a studio.

top3.headline: Perplexity may switch its default model to Gemini Neon
top3.whyItMatters: Model loyalty is weak; vendors switch defaults on retention data alone.

top3.headline: Batching agent branches cut one builder's PRs from 200 to 30 daily
top3.whyItMatters: Agent output is outgrowing CI, so review how your pipeline handles volume.

items.title: Kun Chen: agents are not trained to keep code maintainable
items.takeaway: He says frontier models are rewarded per task in post-training, so agents ignore long-term upkeep. He links this to useless comments and tests.
items.soWhat: Someone on your team still has to own code health after the agent finishes.

items.title: Matt Pocock: written decision records stop agents from guessing
items.takeaway: He says good ADRs matter because agents make assumptions without them. His example came from a session on naming and data relationships.
items.soWhat: Written decisions become the briefing your agents work from.

items.title: Nikita Bier sees a big market for local models on phones
items.takeaway: He argues phone data is too private and too large to send to a frontier model, especially given today's security climate.
items.soWhat: Privacy and security may push some AI work onto the device, away from the cloud.

items.title: Musk calls fine-tuning a chainsaw haircut and system prompts silly
items.takeaway: He says supervised fine-tuning should be part of primary training and that a model's default behaviour should be sensible without a system prompt.
items.soWhat: A lab owner signals that model behaviour should be set in training, not in prompts.

items.title: Nikita Bier: consumer app leaders should not delegate key design calls
items.takeaway: He says building a consumer app takes near-photographic memory of every decision, pixel and data trend. Delegating key design hides new patterns.
items.soWhat: Delegating to agents or teams has a cost: you lose sight of emerging patterns.

items.title: Meng To builds a 3D cyberpunk game in a day with Astra
items.takeaway: In about 24 hours he built a three.js game where you pick a character and drive through a city. He open-sourced three skills: 3D scans, Lens rain, Selector.
items.soWhat: One designer with AI now ships in a day what used to take a studio weeks.

items.title: Perplexity may make Gemini Neon its default model
items.takeaway: Aravind Srinivas says Gemini Neon is live on Perplexity Computer and he hears it beats Opus 5.5. A default switch depends on retention data.
items.soWhat: Default models are chosen on user retention, so expect switches without notice.

items.title: Kun Chen cuts daily PRs from 200 to 30 and ships more
items.takeaway: He now batches several agent branches into one pull request to make CI more efficient, and says he ships more than before.
items.soWhat: With agents writing code, CI capacity, not coding, sets your team's shipping speed.

items.title: Greg Isenberg: build for loneliness and camera-free places
items.takeaway: He lists two big opportunities: real human connection as AI floods everything, and places with no cameras or recording.
items.soWhat: As AI content grows, scarce human and private experiences gain value.

items.title: Theo: source control access should not be all or nothing
items.takeaway: He wants private files inside repos, private branches for small groups and built-in secret management.
items.soWhat: More people and agents in your repos means access needs finer controls.

items.title: poteto suggests /no-comments to strip agent code comments
items.takeaway: He points builders to the /no-comments skill in pstack, or asking your agent to turn it into a lint rule.
items.soWhat: A cheap fix for the noisy comments agents leave in your codebase.

hotOnX.text: The verdict is out: AI was a fad this whole time. $NVDA
hotOnX.note: Sarcasm about the Nvidia sell-off and talk of an AI bubble.

hotOnX.text: Biggest opportunities now: build for loneliness, and for places with no cameras or recording.
hotOnX.note: A popular bet that human connection gains value as AI floods everything.

hotOnX.text: SFT is more like a haircut with a chainsaw; a system prompt is silly. Default behaviour should be sensible.
hotOnX.note: A lab owner's blunt view on how models should be trained.

hotOnX.text: Source control access should not be all-or-nothing: private files, private branches, built-in secrets.
hotOnX.note: Builders want finer repo permissions as agents and teams grow.
